# Reading Níkē the way it was meant to be written
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *nike*. This is the file on how **Níkē** replaced it.

Níkē has few independent myths because she is an attribute of victory rather than a narrative protagonist. But her presence is decisive: she appears at the moment when struggle becomes triumph. In the Theogony (384–385), Styx brings her children Zelos (Rivalry), Nike (Victory), Kratos (Power), and Bia (Force) to Zeús's side at the beginning of the Titanomachy.  Níkē is therefore one of the first divine powers to align with the new Olympian order.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Níkē
- **ASCII form:** nike
- **Meaning:** "Victory, conquest"
- **Domain of influence:** Victory
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Dual-Tier
- **Original script:** Νίκη
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 163 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Νίκη**. On the evidence, it means "Victory, conquest".

Strip **Níkē** to *nike* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **i → í** — Acute on iota: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.
- **e → ē** — Eta: long epsilon: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

These are the small, provable things a restoration is made of: not taste, not branding — attestation.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Níkē** lives at [/sites/nike/](/sites/nike/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/nike/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/nike/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/nike/patterns/).

The name carries both stress and vowel length, and more than one historically valid spelling survives — so the temple presents the pair as a dual-tier restoration, the rarest class in the lexicon.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Níkē** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Sports, Fitness & Competition** — Victory herself; her name became the biggest sports brand in history.
- **Aviation & Aerospace** — Winged and swift, she lent her name to NASA's Nike sounding rockets.
- **Defense, Military & Security** — Project Nike armed America's air defense with missiles bearing her name.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
